title: Spaghetti Carbonara
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale, egg yolk, and Pecorino
excerpt: Spaghetti tossed with crispy guanciale and a sauce of egg yolks and Pecorino Romano that coats every strand in a glossy, rich emulsion. No cream, no shortcuts.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carbonara is a Roman pasta dish of mid-20th century origin, associated with the Lazio region of central Italy. The sauce contains no cream: it is an emulsion of egg yolks and pasta water, enriched by the fat rendered from the guanciale (cured pork cheek) and bound by finely grated Pecorino Romano. The technique requires heating the pasta in the rendered fat and then adding the egg mixture off direct heat, using the residual heat of the pasta and pan to cook the eggs to a silky sauce rather than scrambled eggs. This is the step most home cooks get wrong. The sauce must coat the pasta without scrambling. The pasta water is essential as a thinning and emulsifying agent.

recipeTools.notes: A large pot for the pasta.

content.text: The temperature control is everything. After adding the egg mixture, work quickly off the direct heat: toss and stir constantly, adding splashes of pasta water, until the sauce coats the spaghetti in a glossy emulsion. If the pan is too hot the eggs will scramble. If it is too cool the sauce will be too liquid. The pasta must be cooked and the guanciale must be ready at exactly the same moment. Prepare everything before the pasta goes in.

items.preparation: or Pecorino Romano, very finely grated

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks with the Pecorino and black pepper in a bowl. Set aside.
Cook the spaghetti in a large pot of well-salted boiling water until al dente. Before draining, scoop out 200 ml of the starchy pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, fry the guanciale in a large pan over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the fat has rendered and the pieces are crispy. Remove from the heat.

Drain the pasta. Add to the guanciale pan off the heat. Toss to coat in the fat. Stir 80 ml of pasta water into the egg mixture to temper it. Pour over the pasta and toss vigorously, adding more pasta water a splash at a time, until the sauce is silky and coats every strand. Serve immediately.
